data.title: Accertify Expands Fraud Prevention Capabilities into Healthcare with HIPAA Compliance
data.ai_summary: Accertify announced it has achieved HIPAA compliance, allowing healthcare organizations, HSA providers, pharmacies and healthcare-adjacent businesses to use its AI-powered Predictive Yes fraud prevention platform while safeguarding protected health information. The company cited healthcare fraud costing tens of billions annually and HSA assets near $174 billion at the end of 2025.
data.full_text:
ⓘ This article is third-party content and does not represent the views of this site. We make no guarantees regarding its accuracy or completeness.

HIPAA compliance enables healthcare organizations, HSA providers, pharmacies, and healthcare-adjacent businesses to leverage Accertify's AI-powered fraud prevention platform while meeting rigorous privacy and security requirements

Accertify, a leading fraud decisioning provider whose Predictive Yes Platform helps merchants say yes to more good customers, more revenue, and more growth, today announced it has achieved HIPAA compliance, expanding the company's ability to help healthcare organizations and healthcare-adjacent businesses combat payment fraud, account takeover, and other forms of digital healthcare fraud while safeguarding protected health information (PHI).

Healthcare fraud costs the industry tens of billions of dollars annually and increasingly extends beyond traditional claims fraud into digital payments, account access, and ecommerce. At the same time, the Health Savings Account (HSA) market continues to expand rapidly, reaching nearly 42 million accounts holding approximately $174 billion in assets at the end of 2025, according to research from Devenir. As HSA cards become a more common payment method for healthcare purchases, they also present an increasingly attractive target for account takeover, stolen credentials, and payment fraud.

Achieving HIPAA compliance expands Accertify's ability to help healthcare organizations apply enterprise-grade fraud prevention across digital payment journeys involving protected health information. The company can now support a broader range of healthcare and healthcare-adjacent organizations, including HSA issuers, pharmacies, insurers, and medical supply retailers, while meeting the privacy and security standards required to safeguard sensitive patient data.

"Healthcare organizations are rapidly digitizing the way consumers pay for care, prescriptions, and other qualified expenses," said Andy Mortland, Vice President of Product and Development at Accertify. "As healthcare payments become more connected and HSA adoption continues to grow, fraudsters are following the money. Organizations need fraud prevention that protects consumers without creating friction at the moments that matter most."

For healthcare payment organizations, that balance between fraud prevention, privacy, and customer experience is becoming increasingly critical.

As healthcare organizations, pharmacies, and healthcare retailers continue expanding digital payment options, Accertify's Predictive Yes Platform helps them confidently approve legitimate healthcare purchases while detecting fraud across the customer journey, enabling organizations to protect consumers, preserve trust, and grow revenue without introducing unnecessary friction.

About Accertify

Accertify enables commerce by doing one thing extraordinarily well: pinpointing fraud. The company's Predictive Yes Platform helps businesses say yes to more - more good customers, more revenue, and more growth - without getting burned. It's a precise, confident, data-backed yes, made possible by joining signals across the entire customer lifecycle through unmatched data volume, layered AI-powered models, and a consortium approach that protects clients from bad actors spotted anywhere in the network while unlocking business with good actors verified anywhere in the network. With more than 10 billion transactions and over $1 trillion in commerce processed in 2025 alone, Accertify delivers the intelligence and precision that fraud and payments teams need to say yes confidently and enable growth. That's the More Yes difference. Learn more at accertify.com.

data.title: Accertify Sets Bold Vision for “More Yes” – a New Era of AI-Powered Commerce Enablement
data.ai_summary: Accertify announced the Predictive Yes Platform, a new enterprise fraud decisioning technology that connects identity, behavioral, and purchase signals across the full customer lifecycle from account creation through post-purchase. The platform leverages data from over 10 billion transactions and $1.25 trillion in commerce processed annually, alongside a consortium approach where 98% of clients share anonymized fraud intelligence across retail, travel, and other sectors. New AI enhancements include machine learning for automated manual review, graph network capabilities for real-time fraud ring detection, and industry-specific AI models for deeper vertical precision.
data.author: Business Wire

industries.name: Verification & Risk Signals (Device Fingerprinting, Behavioral Biometrics)

data.full_text:
To reflect its connected, continuous ML-based fraud decisioning capabilities across the full customer lifecycle, Accertify’s platform is now the Predictive Yes Platform

ITASCA, Ill.–(BUSINESS WIRE)–The fraud problem has shifted. For years, merchants have focused their fraud defenses at checkout, at the moment of transaction. Meanwhile fraudsters have shifted their attack methods, exploiting account creation, login, and account changes long before a purchase is made. At the same time, the explosion of first-party abuse – like refund fraud, promotion gaming, and policy exploitation by people who look exactly like legitimate customers – has extended fraud risk past the point of payment. Against this backdrop, a convergence between fraud and cybersecurity is occurring as the two disciplines join forces and work together on account takeover, identity confidence, and card not present (CNP) fraud. This convergence recognizes that fraudsters are treating the entire customer lifecycle as a single attack surface. In the meantime, businesses must still drive growth. Accertify, Inc. today announced the Predictive Yes Platform, a new category of enterprise technology that addresses these challenges by joining identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals across the full customer lifecycle and decisioning on them continuously, from the moment a customer arrives to long after they’ve checked out. The platform makes possible a new kind of yes: not reckless, not naive, but precise, confident, and data-backed. That is the vision Accertify calls “More Yes.” “Fraudsters don’t respect org charts,” said Greg Dukat, CEO of Accertify. “They treat account creation, login, checkout, and post-purchase as one continuous attack surface. The Predictive Yes Platform is built the same way – one connected system across the full customer lifecycle, so businesses can approve more good customers with confidence and fuel growth – without the wrong people coming along for the ride.” The Predictive Yes Platform The Predictive Yes Platform connects signals that have historically lived in silos – identity signals at account creation, behavioral signals at login and account change, browsing and shopping signals at consideration, purchase signals at checkout, and outcome signals through returns, refunds, and chargebacks – into a single, continuously learning view of each customer. Rather than making isolated decisions at individual transaction points, the platform decisions risk at every stage of the journey, so that by the time a good customer reaches checkout, the answer is already clear. That intelligence is fueled by three structural advantages. The first is data at scale: Over the past 12-month period from May 1, 2025, to April 30, 2026, according to Accertify client data, the company processed more than 10 billion transactions representing $1.25 trillion in commerce.

The second is a consortium approach in which 98% of Accertify clients have opted in to share anonymized fraud intelligence across hundreds of enterprise brands in retail, travel, regulated gaming, entertainment and media, restaurants, ticketing, financial services, and other sectors – so a pattern identified anywhere in the network protects everyone, and a trusted customer verified anywhere moves faster everywhere.

The third is layered AI-powered models, from decision trees to supervised machine learning to graph networks and more – each purpose-built for specific fraud types and using industry-specific signals – working in concert to stay ahead of evolving attacks. Those advantages are continuously extended through platform innovation. Accertify’s most recent enhancements put AI at the center of decisioning in new ways. A new AI-driven capability applies machine learning to the manual review queue before a human analyst ever sees it, automating a significant portion of reviews and reducing the over-marking that costs merchants good customers. Graph network capabilities now bring real-time detection of fraud rings and coordinated attacks by mapping complex, non-linear relationships between identities, devices, behaviors, and transactions. And updated industry-specific AI models bring deeper vertical signal training to bear, improving precision for Accertify’s largest client segments. The company’s Predictive Yes Platform helps businesses say yes to more – more good customers, more revenue, and more growth – without getting burned. Accertify Sets Bold Vision for “More Yes” – a New Era of AI-Powered Commerce Enablement

Share

To reflect its connected, continuous ML-based fraud decisioning capabilities across the full customer lifecycle, Accertify’s platform is now the Predictive Yes Platform

ITASCA, Ill.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--The fraud problem has shifted. For years, merchants have focused their fraud defenses at checkout, at the moment of transaction. Meanwhile fraudsters have shifted their attack methods, exploiting account creation, login, and account changes long before a purchase is made. At the same time, the explosion of first-party abuse - like refund fraud, promotion gaming, and policy exploitation by people who look exactly like legitimate customers - has extended fraud risk past the point of payment. Against this backdrop, a convergence between fraud and cybersecurity is occurring as the two disciplines join forces and work together on account takeover, identity confidence, and card not present (CNP) fraud. This convergence recognizes that fraudsters are treating the entire customer lifecycle as a single attack surface. In the meantime, businesses must still drive growth. Accertify, Inc. today announced the Predictive Yes Platform, a new category of enterprise technology that addresses these challenges by joining identity, behavioral, historical, and purchase signals across the full customer lifecycle and decisioning on them continuously, from the moment a customer arrives to long after they've checked out. The platform makes possible a new kind of yes: not reckless, not naive, but precise, confident, and data-backed. That is the vision Accertify calls "More Yes." “Fraudsters don’t respect org charts,” said Greg Dukat, CEO of Accertify. “They treat account creation, login, checkout, and post-purchase as one continuous attack surface. The Predictive Yes Platform is built the same way - one connected system across the full customer lifecycle, so businesses can approve more good customers with confidence and fuel growth - without the wrong people coming along for the ride.” The Predictive Yes Platform The Predictive Yes Platform connects signals that have historically lived in silos - identity signals at account creation, behavioral signals at login and account change, browsing and shopping signals at consideration, purchase signals at checkout, and outcome signals through returns, refunds, and chargebacks - into a single, continuously learning view of each customer. Rather than making isolated decisions at individual transaction points, the platform decisions risk at every stage of the journey, so that by the time a good customer reaches checkout, the answer is already clear. That intelligence is fueled by three structural advantages. The first is data at scale: Over the past 12-month period from May 1, 2025, to April 30, 2026, according to Accertify client data, the company processed more than 10 billion transactions representing $1.25 trillion in commerce.

The second is a consortium approach in which 98% of Accertify clients have opted in to share anonymized fraud intelligence across hundreds of enterprise brands in retail, travel, regulated gaming, entertainment and media, restaurants, ticketing, financial services, and other sectors - so a pattern identified anywhere in the network protects everyone, and a trusted customer verified anywhere moves faster everywhere.

The third is layered AI-powered models, from decision trees to supervised machine learning to graph networks and more - each purpose-built for specific fraud types and using industry-specific signals - working in concert to stay ahead of evolving attacks. Those advantages are continuously extended through platform innovation. Accertify's most recent enhancements put AI at the center of decisioning in new ways. A new AI-driven capability applies machine learning to the manual review queue before a human analyst ever sees it, automating a significant portion of reviews and reducing the over-marking that costs merchants good customers. Graph network capabilities now bring real-time detection of fraud rings and coordinated attacks by mapping complex, non-linear relationships between identities, devices, behaviors, and transactions. And updated industry-specific AI models bring deeper vertical signal training to bear, improving precision for Accertify's largest client segments. data.title: Accertify’s Attack State Combats Coordinated Login Attacks
data.ai_summary: Accertify announced the launch of Attack State, a new capability within its Account Protection solution designed to detect and respond to coordinated login attacks and automated threats targeting customer accounts. The solution continuously analyzes login activity against broader traffic patterns to identify anomalies associated with bot-driven campaigns, credential stuffing, and account takeover attempts, providing both fraud and cybersecurity teams with automated alerts and contextual intelligence. Accertify will present Attack State at MRC Vegas 2026, taking place March 16-19.
data.author: Tony Zerucha
data.full_text:
Accertify, a unified risk decisioning platform provider, today announced the launch of Attack State, a new capability within its Account Protection solution that helps organizations detect and respond to coordinated login attacks and other automated threats targeting customer accounts.

Attack State analyzes login activity continuously and compares it to the organization’s broader traffic patterns to determine when a client’s environment may be under active attack. By comparing expected network behavior with real-time activity, the capability identifies anomalies associated with bot-driven campaigns, credential stuffing, and account takeover attempts.

Attack State provides both fraud and cybersecurity teams with greater visibility into account access attempts across web, mobile, and API environments. When abnormal activity is detected, Attack State surfaces alerts and contextual intelligence automatically, helping cybersecurity teams assess potential threats, monitor system performance, and adjust perimeter defenses if necessary.

For fraud prevention teams, the benefit is earlier awareness of attacks that may otherwise go unnoticed until downstream fraud or account compromise occurs. Additionally, Attack State allows Accertify’s models to adjust to the traffic anomaly and continue to allow good users through while blocking malicious bad actors.

“Customer accounts are one of the most valuable targets for attackers today,” said Andy Mortland, senior vice president of product and development, Accertify. “This is why we must broaden fraud controls beyond the point of checkout alone. Organizations need visibility into signals across the entire customer journey, from login activity to transactions to post-purchase.

“Attack State is an example of the power of taking a holistic, platform approach to fraud, one that connects early attack signals with downstream fraud decisioning, giving fraud and cybersecurity teams the context they need to respond faster and protect customer accounts.”

Accertify will be presenting Attack State during a workshop titled, Protecting Accounts Before Fraud Reaches Checkout, at MRC Vegas 2026, taking place March 16-19. Accertify is also a sponsor and exhibitor of the conference. Please visit booth #211 to meet with the Accertify team at the event to learn more.
